headline: Gold lost the $4,000 handle and VIX jumped 7.8% overnight — the one-headline AI bounce is stalling right as a reopened bond market reprices a hot core CPI.
summary: The relief lasted one session. VIX is +7.8% to 18.86 today after yesterday's -10.1%, the VIX/VIX3M term structure is back to 0.909 and turning up, and Asia handed back the bounce: TAIEX -2.6% after a +3.6% week, Nikkei -0.7% (-10.3% on the month, z=-2.18), KOSPI -0.6%, Hang Seng -1.3%, Euro Stoxx -0.2%. US cash is still stamped 11 Nov (SPX 7,619.4 +1.3%, NDX +2.3%, SOXX +6.0%, MU +11.9%), so the tape you see is a bounce that the rest of the world has already started selling. Risk regime -13 versus -10 yesterday; credit & vol composite -39.

The new damage is in the metals and it is mechanical, not cyclical. Gold -2.3% to 3,906.9, now -6.5% on the month, 12.9% below its 200-day and at the 0.6th percentile of its year. Silver -2.8% to 50.44, -14.7% on the month, 27% below its 200-day, 2nd percentile. Platinum 6.5th percentile. Gold/silver +9.7% on the month at z=1.42. The driver is a 10-year real yield of 2.66 sitting 19% above its 200-day against a dollar at the 100th percentile: DXY 102.93, EURUSD 1.1088 at the 0th percentile and -0.7% today, GBP -0.7%, AUD -0.6%, USDCHF +0.9%, USDJPY 159.76 and turning up. The fracture point is still Brazil: USDBRL 5.6045, +12.4% on the month at z=3.55 with acceleration +2.88, EWZ -25.5% on the month, Bovespa z=-3.35 — while Mexico's IPC sits at the 100th percentile and India's Sensex is +12.2% at z=2.91.

Rates reopen into a bear flattener the equity bounce never priced. 2s10s -7bp to 25bp, the 9th percentile of the year; 3-month bills +5bp to 4.24, 2-year +5bp to 4.56, 10-year 4.88, MOVE +7.5% to 92.4. Core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 with the index at the 100th percentile, yet 10-year breakevens are 2.20 at the 6th percentile and 5-year 2.25. That is the live mispricing. Credit gave a clean day — HY OAS -8bp to 3.34, CCC -6bp, BBB -3bp, IG -2bp, BKLN at the 99th percentile — but spreads are still +23bp (HY) and +58bp (CCC) wider on the month, with IG at z=1.19 and BBB z=1.34. Liquidity is no help: net liquidity rolling over, bank reserves -0.6% on the month, RRP functionally zero at $0.15bn.

Underneath, the rotation is at both tails and it is not a growth scare. Growth/value z=-2.66 at the 9th percentile, high-beta/low-vol z=-2.35, MTUM z=-2.25, SMH/SPY z=-2.04, NVDA -23.2% on the month at the 12th percentile — against RSP/SPY at z=3.4 with acceleration +3.06, XRT/SPY z=2.48, HD z=2.86 (+20.9%), MCD z=3.16, LLY +21.5%, LMT +19.2%, UPS +17.9%, XLV at the 98.5th percentile. The economy is fine: claims 200k, continuing claims at the 1st percentile, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%, industrial production +0.63. What is broken is the electron chain feeding the AI build — GEV -18.9%, VST -15.6%, ETN -15.2%, GRID -9.0% on the month while the chips ripped — and the industrial metals, copper -7.3% on the month with COPX -14.0% and FCX -15.1%. Energy is the one commodity turning the other way: Brent +1.5% to 94.11 and turning up, WTI +1.0% to 87.4, XOP +2.6%, OIH +2.8%.

good.text: Credit refused to confirm the equity wobble: HY OAS -8bp to 3.34, CCC -6bp to 13.11, BBB -3bp, IG -2bp, HYG +0.2%, HYG/IEF turning up and BKLN at the 99th percentile of its year. Spread markets are not pricing a funding accident.

Breadth is the strongest signal on the board: RSP/SPY z=3.4 with acceleration +3.06, equal-weight S&P +4.4% on the month at the 98.5th percentile, Dow Transports +4.6% and turning up, IWM turning up. The index pain is concentration, not participation.

No recession under the unwind: initial claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), industrial production +0.63 and capacity utilization at a 52-week high.

Leadership has migrated offshore to the right places: DAX at the 100th percentile (+5.7% 1m), CAC +6.7%, Sensex +12.2% at z=2.91, INDA +11.3% with acceleration +2.54, Mexico's IPC at the 100th percentile and EWW +6.1%.
Energy is turning up while every other commodity sags: Brent +1.5% to 94.11 (trend turning up), WTI +1.0% to 87.4, XOP +2.6%, OIH +2.8%, XLE +1.9% with 3-month relative strength +5.9%.

The semiconductor complex found a bid with real size: SOXX +6.0%, MU +11.9%, AMD +7.3%, ORCL +8.8%, TSM +4.3%. Washed-out positioning (SMH/SPY z=-2.04) means these squeezes can run even inside a downtrend.

bad.text: Vol is re-igniting, not decaying: VIX +7.8% to 18.86 and turning up, +23.5% on the month, with the VIX/VIX3M term structure at 0.909 and rising (z=0.76). Yesterday's -10.1% collapse in VIX has been fully retraced.

Gold broke $4,000: -2.3% to 3,906.9, -6.5% on the month, 12.9% below its 200-day, 0.6th percentile of the year. Silver -2.8% to 50.44 and 27% below its 200-day, platinum at the 6.5th percentile. With the 10-year real yield at 2.66 — 19% above its 200-day — this is a real-rate squeeze, and it is accelerating, not stabilizing.

The dollar is a wrecking ball at the 100th percentile: DXY 102.93, EURUSD 1.1088 at the 0th percentile, GBP -0.7%, AUD -0.6%, USDCHF +0.9%, USDJPY 159.76 and turning up into intervention territory. USDBRL 5.6045 at z=3.55 with acceleration +2.88 is a full-blown funding dislocation, not a wobble.

Bear flattening with inflation underpriced: 2s10s -7bp to 25bp (9th percentile), 3m bills +5bp to 4.24, 2y +5bp to 4.56, MOVE +7.5% to 92.4 — while core CPI turns up at z=0.93 and 10-year breakevens sit at 2.20, the 6th percentile. The bond market reopens into this today.

Crypto is bleeding on a day stocks were supposed to be recovering: BTC -1.8% to 72,622 (-12.6% 1m), ETH -2.0% (-19.3% 1m), SOL -23.5% on the month, COIN at the 2nd percentile. Net liquidity is rolling over, bank reserves -0.6% on the month and RRP is empty at $0.15bn — the marginal-dollar bid is gone.

The industrial and AI-power complex keeps breaking: copper -1.3% today and -7.3% on the month, COPX -14.0%, FCX -15.1%, XME -7.3%; GEV -18.9%, VST -15.6%, GRID -9.0% on the month. Hang Seng -1.3% and Shanghai at the 8th percentile cap the demand side.

trades.name: Short TLT into the bond-market reopen
trades.line: Short TLT into the reopen: bear flattener, core CPI turning up
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy Dec 82 puts financed by selling 86 calls. Size 1x book risk.
trades.thesis: The equity bounce was priced with Treasuries shut. The front end is already repricing hawkish — fed funds 3.88, 3m bills 4.24 (+5bp), 2y 4.56 (+5bp) — while core CPI turns up at z=0.93 and 10y breakevens sit at 2.20, the 6th percentile. TLT rallied 4.1% on the month into that. Duration is the wrong side of a hot-inflation, flat-curve regime.
trades.trigger: 2s10s -7bp to 25bp (9th percentile), MOVE +7.5% to 92.4, 10y 4.88 with real yields 19% above the 200-day; TLT up 4.1% on the month on a shortened, illiquid week.
trades.stop: TLT above 83.5 (10y back under 4.70) or a 2s10s re-steepening above 40bp on a dovish repricing.

trades.name: Long India vs short Brazil
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWZ: EM dispersion, BRL still blowing out
trades.thesis: EM is no longer one asset class. India has a strengthening currency (USDINR -1.8% on the month, z=-1.87) and the strongest equity momentum in the digest; Brazil has a currency in freefall and an index at z=-3.35. A 100th-percentile dollar keeps punishing the high-carry, high-deficit leg and rewarding the one with falling import costs as oil's month-long -11% Brent move cheapens India's energy bill.
trades.trigger: INDA +11.3% on the month at z=2.55 with acceleration +2.54 and Sensex z=2.91, against EWZ -25.5% on the month (z=-3.33, acceleration -3.37) and USDBRL +12.4% at z=3.55, still accelerating today (+0.4%).
trades.stop: USDBRL back under 5.35 with Bovespa reclaiming its 200-day, or the pair down 6%.
trades.target: +10% on the pair as BRL stress bleeds into Brazilian equity multiples.

trades.name: Short crypto beta as the liquidity canary
trades.line: Short ETH/SOL: crypto is the liquidity canary, not a dip
trades.expr: Short ETH 1x and SOL 0.5x via perps or futures; alternatively short MSTR as the levered equity proxy.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the purest read on marginal liquidity and it is failing on days equities rally. RRP is exhausted at $0.15bn, bank reserves -0.6% on the month and net liquidity is rolling over. The high-beta tail of the complex (ETH, SOL) is underperforming bitcoin — ETH/BTC at the 19th percentile and -7.7% on the month — which is how these drawdowns extend, not end.
trades.trigger: BTC -1.8% to 72,622 (-12.6% 1m), ETH -2.0% (-19.3% 1m), SOL -2.0% (-23.5% 1m), COIN at the 2nd percentile of its year and MSTR -14.2% on the week, all while SPX printed +1.3%.
trades.stop: ETH back above 2,300 with ETH/BTC turning up, or a 12% loss on the combined short.
trades.target: ETH toward 1,700, SOL toward 65; +18% on the position.

trades.name: Long E&P equity as the cheap inflation hedge
trades.line: Long XOP: oil turning up, breakevens at the 6th percentile
trades.expr: Long XOP 1x with XLE 0.5x as ballast; sell Jan calls 10% out if you want carry.
trades.thesis: Breakevens at 2.20 (6th percentile) with core CPI turning up is the cleanest mispricing on the board, and energy equity is the liquid way to own it. Crude is turning up off a washed-out month while the equity never followed oil's +7.6% three-month move — XOP is -7.3% on the month at z=-1.02. Gold just failed as the inflation hedge; oil is where the hedge is cheap.
trades.trigger: Brent +1.5% to 94.11 and flipping to turning_up, WTI +1.0% to 87.4, XOP +2.6%, OIH +2.8%, XLE +1.9% with 3-month relative strength +5.9% versus the S&P.
trades.stop: Brent closing below 88 (back under the 200-day) or the position down 8%.
trades.target: +12%, XOP back to its early-October highs as crude retakes 98 Brent.

trades.name: Long gold vs short silver
trades.line: Long GLD vs short SILVER: real-rate squeeze hits silver harder
trades.expr: Long GLD, short silver futures/SLV, dollar-neutral 1:1.
trades.thesis: If you must own the precious complex through a real-rate squeeze, own the monetary leg and short the industrial one. Silver carries both the real-yield hit and the industrial demand hit that copper is already flagging; it is 27% below its 200-day with no floor in sight. The ratio has trended up for three months and still has the macro behind it: real yield 2.66, 19% above its 200-day, and a dollar at the 100th percentile.
trades.trigger: Gold/silver +9.7% on the month at z=1.42 and trending up; silver -14.7% on the month versus gold -6.5%, with copper -1.3% today and -7.3% on the month confirming the industrial-demand side.
trades.stop: Gold/silver back below 72, or the pair down 6% — a dollar reversal would lift silver hardest.

trades.name: Long healthcare vs short semis
trades.line: Long XLV vs short SMH: fade the one-headline chip bounce
trades.expr: Long XLV, short SMH, dollar-neutral 1:1; use IBB/LLY if you prefer the pharma tilt.
trades.thesis: The chip rally was one AI-infrastructure headline against a tape where SMH/SPY is at z=-2.04 and -12.2% relative on the month, NVDA is -23.2% at the 12th percentile, and the power chain that funds the capex (GEV -18.9%, VST -15.6%, GRID -9.0%) is still broken. Healthcare is the opposite: XLV +9.9% on the month at z=2.29, 98.5th percentile, relative strength +12.5%/+14.2% and trending up, led by LLY +21.5%.
trades.trigger: SOXX +6.0% and MU +11.9% in a single session with SMH still rolling over and 2.9% below its 200-day, while XLV relative strength keeps making highs.
trades.stop: SMH reclaims its 200-day with SMH/SPY turning up, or the pair down 7% — XLV is already 18.9% above its own 200-day, so the long leg is extended.

trades.name: Short AUDUSD on the copper rollover
trades.line: Short AUDUSD: copper rolling over, dollar at 100th pctile
trades.expr: Short AUDUSD spot/futures, or buy 3-month 0.6700 puts.
trades.thesis: The Aussie is the cleanest liquid short against both legs of today's macro: a dollar at the 100th percentile and a China/industrial-metals complex that keeps deteriorating. Unlike EM crosses, there is no carry penalty and no intervention risk.
trades.trigger: AUDUSD -0.6% to 0.68273, -2.5% on the week and -1.9% on the month (z=-0.70); copper -1.3% today and -7.3% on the month, Hang Seng -1.3%, Shanghai at the 8th percentile, AUD/JPY rolling over.
trades.stop: 0.6950 — a reclaim of the 200-day with copper back above 6.50.
